verdict: The instruments, hours and order events exist and are tradable, and the package's commission-plus-tick cost assumptions hold on the right account type (MNQ 0.16-0.48 bp vs 0.83 assumed; mini K200 0.28-0.49 bp vs 0.6 at KIS BanKIS or Kiwoom, but 1.08-1.17 bp on a KIS branch-type account). The package is NOT executable as specified on margin grounds. At current margins (KRX mini K200 21% initial / 14% maintenance since 2026-11-02; MNQ maintenance about $4,516 = 7.25% of notional) the cap position needs 82.3M KRW of initial margin against 80M of capital. The 30M domestic account can open only 2 mini contracts (1.32x), or 3 (1.98x) with the 10M reserve, not 3x. The package's own margin_ok (x1.6 buffer) would cut to 3 MNQ + 1 mini. For the US leg at 5x in a 40M account, a margin call comes at NDX -2.75% and real-time forced liquidation (risk 80% at both Kiwoom and KIS, charged at offline rates) at -8.4%. Applying today's margin to history with the raw rule leverage, the US account falls below maintenance at the open 19 times in 27.6 years and gets a settlement margin call 61 times (2.2/yr). The backtest excluded forced liquidation, margin limits and FX, so its 5x/3x results do not transfer to live trading without re-simulation under margin constraints. Only KIS REST covers both legs by API; Kiwoom futures need the Windows-only OCX. Fill slippage at the four order times was not measured by anyone.

findings.title: Cap leverage cannot be carried with the 40M/30M/10M split at current margins
findings.detail: KRX raised mini K200 margin to 21% initial / 14% maintenance effective 2026-11-02 (it was 9.15% / 6.10% in Sept 2025). Caps of 5x MNQ + 3x mini on 80M need 31.88M + 50.40M = 82.28M KRW initial margin, more than total capital. The 30M domestic account opens at most 2 mini (1.32x of equity), or 3 (1.98x) using the whole 10M reserve; the current raw rule target of 2.5x (3 contracts, 33.28M) already does not fit in 30M. The plan and demo code implicitly assumed about 12% (K200) and 8% (MNQ). Live leverage will be well below backtest leverage on the KR leg whenever its target exceeds about 1.8x.

findings.title: Forced liquidation is real-time at both brokers and sits inside the historical range of moves
findings.detail: Kiwoom and KIS both liquidate overseas futures at market when risk reaches 80% (equity = 20% of initial margin), with SMS notice only, and KIS states liquidation is not its obligation. Margin calls are set at daily settlement when equity is below maintenance. For 5x in a 40M account: call at -2.75%, liquidation at -8.41% (5 whole contracts: -2.33% / -7.98%). At raw rule leverage with today's margin, the account is below maintenance at the open on 19 nights in 27.6 years and gets 61 settlement calls (2.2/yr); the 80% line is reached at the RTH low on 2010-05-06 and 2015-08-24. Close-to-open data cannot see intra-night lows, so these are lower bounds for the night leg. The package states forced liquidation was not simulated.

findings.title: Margins rise in stress and can trigger calls without a price move
findings.detail: CME equity index margins have been on SPAN2 since 2024-10-18 and can change daily. MNQ initial went $2,442 to $3,410 (+40%) between 2025-04-09 and 2025-04-23. At the 2020-03-18 level (about 10.5% maintenance) 5x would need 41.8M maintenance against a 40M account. Kiwoom applies changes on Tuesdays and says a hike triggers real-time liquidation and additional margin at the open. K200 initial margin went 9.15% to 21% in 13 months. Mitigation: the vol target usually cuts leverage before sustained stress (0.5x on 2020-03-16), so the exposure is the first shock night from a calm regime (2015-08-24, 2024-08-05, 2025-04-03 were all at 5x).

findings.title: Plan contract counts and notionals are stale; one MNQ exceeds 1.0x of total equity
findings.detail: At project data prices one MNQ is 83.6M KRW (1.04x of 80M) and one mini K200 is 52.8M (0.66x); the plan says 76M and 39.5M. The 5x cap is 4 MNQ (4.18x), the 4x day cap is 3 MNQ, the 3x KR cap is 4 mini. The 0.5-step leverage grid cannot be expressed in whole contracts at this account size: 4.5x and 4.0x both give 4 or 3 contracts, 2.5x gives 2. The task premise of 5 MNQ + 6 mini would be 5.22x and 3.96x.

findings.title: API coverage: only KIS REST handles both legs; Kiwoom futures are Windows-only OCX
findings.detail: Kiwoom REST API covers domestic stocks, ETF/ETN/ELW, gold spot and US stocks only. KOSPI200 futures need Kiwoom OpenAPI+ and overseas futures need the separate overseas-derivatives OpenAPI+, both Windows PC programs. A secondary source citing a Kiwoom board answer says the Kiwoom API does not support the KRX night session. KIS Open API (REST/WebSocket) has domestic futures day and night order TRs and overseas futures order TRs. No paper-trading TR for overseas futures appears in the catalog I saw, so MNQ mock trading by API is probably unavailable (inferred).

findings.title: Costs: package assumptions hold for commission plus tick, but depend on account type and unmeasured slippage
findings.detail: MNQ: 0.16-0.48 bp one-way including up to 2 ticks, against 0.83 bp assumed, so the US assumption is conservative at today's index level. Mini K200: KIS BanKIS 0.00185% and Kiwoom 0.003% give 0.37-0.49 bp with 1 tick, under 0.6 bp with only about 2 ticks of room; a KIS branch-type account at 0.009811% gives 1.17 bp, above both the 0.6 bp assumption and the plan's 0.9 bp go-live threshold. No spread or depth data exists for 09:00:05 / 15:30:20 KST or 16:00:20 / 09:30:05 ET; the package itself calls execution cost the largest variable. One-off KRW to USD conversion spread is not in the cost model.

findings.title: Broker rules differ on what counts as collateral
findings.detail: Kiwoom computes overseas-futures risk separately per deposit currency, so KRW sitting in the account would not protect a USD position. KIS computes on total assets converted to KRW, but covers a foreign-currency shortfall at a rate 5% worse than the base rate and auto-converts at 09:00. KIS margin-call deadline is 16:00 KST, liquidation by limit order 20 ticks adverse. KIS has no basic deposit for overseas derivatives; Kiwoom's is unverified.

findings.title: KRX account rules: basic deposit is re-checked daily for this strategy; intraday margin calls exist
findings.detail: Futures need a basic deposit of at least 10M KRW (broker sets the tier), 1 hour of pre-education and 3 hours of mock trading. The deposit is checked when opening from flat, which this strategy does every afternoon. Additional margin is due by 12:00 next trading day when equity is below maintenance at the close; an intraday additional margin applies when KOSPI200 moves at least 80% of the maintenance rate (11.2% now), due 08:00 next day, and is not applied in the night session. Non-payment leads to liquidation without notice.

findings.title: Order-time and calendar issues
findings.detail: E2 at 15:30:20 KST leaves 4m40s before the 15:35 closing auction. KRX futures open at 08:45, so E1 at 09:00:05 is 15 minutes into continuous trading and only the +/-8% limit applies 08:45-09:00. On CME half days the market closes 13:15 ET, so E3 cannot run at 16:00:20. KIS force-closes cash-settled overseas contracts at 16:00 KST the day before last trading day unless consent is given, so the MNQ roll must be earlier. KRX has its own night session since 2025-06-09 (18:00-06:00), which gives a way to cut the KR leg overnight that the backtest does not use. E3/E4 are ET-anchored, so the scheduler must handle US daylight saving.

findings.title: Live skeleton code is not broker-ready
findings.detail: v11_live.py takes market data from a Yahoo class, uses a paper broker with fixed 12% / 8% margins, and computes total equity as the two futures accounts only, leaving out the separate cash account. Margin, quotes and equity must come from the broker API before any live use.

findings.title: Interest assumptions are unverified
findings.detail: The package assumes 0 on USD (conservative) and Korean rate minus 0.3%p on 50% of the KR margin. Sources conflict on USD: a KIS fee page shows 0.70% above $500 as of 2026-01-01, while a 2026-09 article and an older KIS page say 0% for overseas-futures accounts; Kiwoom is reported at 0.45-0.6% above $1,000. I found no source for KRW deposit interest in a domestic futures account, so the minus 0.3%p assumption may be optimistic.

findings.title: Tax treatment matches the package
findings.detail: 11% including local tax, 2.5M KRW deduction, domestic and overseas derivatives netted since 2017, no loss carry-forward, annual filing in May, FIFO, overseas P&L converted at the settlement-date base rate. The package ignores the deduction, which is conservative. The financial investment income tax was abolished on 2024-12-10, so this regime continues.
